J." Wilson''' (born February 19, 1996) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played college basketball for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]] and completed his junior season for the [[2016–17 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2016–17 team]]. He has entered his name for the [[2017 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== At Capital Christian School in Sacramento, Wilson endured a fifth [[lumbar vertebrae|lumbar vertebra]] [[stress fracture]], which sidelined him during the summer of 2012 and part of his junior season, which caused him to lose the attention of some recruiters. He spent three months in a back brace from his hips to his chest. By the middle of his junior season, he completed a 1-year 5-inch growth spurt that took him to a height of {{convert|6|ft|8|in|m|2}}. By June 2013, he had recovered enough to tally 22 [[point (basketball)|points]] and 8 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] against [[Ivan Rabb]] at a [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|California Golden Bears]] camp event at [[Haas Pavilion]]. Soon thereafter, Michigan and other schools began recruiting him. [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|The defending 2013 national runner-up Wolverines]] hosted him (and [[Devin Booker]]) during the first weekend of October 2013 and he accepted Michigan over offers from [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]], [[Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball|Northwestern]], and [[Harvard Crimson men's basketball|Harvard]].{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2013/10/michigan_hoops_commit_dj_wilso.html|title=Michigan hoops commit D.J. Wilson took advantage of 'defining moment' in recruitment|accessdate=April 5, 2017|date=October 7, 2013|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}} Wilson signed his [[National Letter of Intent]] with Michigan on November 13, 2013, with the expectation that [[Jordan Morgan]] would graduate from the [[2013–14 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2013–14 Wolverines team]] and both [[Glenn Robinson III]] and [[Mitch McGary]] would enter the [[2014 NBA draft]]. At the time of his signing, he was believed to be the first [[Sacramento metropolitan area|Sacramento area]] player to ever sign with a [[Big Ten Conference]] school.{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2013/11/dj_wilson_submits_nli_becomes.html|title=D.J. Wilson submits NLI, becomes second official member of Michigan basketball's 2014 class|accessdate=November 17, 2013|date=November 13, 2013|publisher=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}} {{College athlete recruit start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2014}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = D. Wilson, Max Bielfeld back from injury, cleared to play as practice begins|accessdate=April 4, 2017|date=October 3, 2014|website=[[MLive.com]]|author=Quinn, Brendan F.}} During the fifth game of the season for the [[2014–15 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2014–15 team]] against [[2014–15 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]] in the 2014 [[Legends Classic (basketball tournament)|Legends Classic]], Wilson was injured when he was blocked and knocked down on a [[slam dunk]] attempt against Dylan Ennis. He was sidelined due to a sprained knee and eventually missed the remainder of the season.
